create.name: Ārsha Vidyā Paramparā
create.bio:
Ārsha Vidyā Paramparā is a charitable trust in India that teaches Advaita Vedanta in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati, reading the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita through Adi Shankara's commentaries. Its teacher is Swami Sarvananda Saraswati, who studied Vedanta and Sanskrit at Arsha Vijnana Gurukulam in Nagpur and then at Arsha Vidya Gurukulam in Coimbatore, where he also taught, after earlier years working in information technology in India and the United States.

Classes run live on Zoom at weekends on Indian time: a long verse-by-verse cycle through the Gita, the Mundaka Upanishad and Vidyaranya's Panchadashi, each followed by questions. The trust also holds residential camps and retreats, in India and in Scandinavia, that pair classes with guided meditation and bhajans, and it is building Ātma Vidyā Gurukulam, a small residential study centre near Hosur in Tamil Nadu. The YouTube channel, started in 2017, carries whole class series, such as an eight-part enquiry into 'Who am I', a session-by-session reading of Bhaja Govindam and the closing chapter of the Gita, along with short talks on ideas such as the three gunas.

courses.title: Online Bhagavad Gita, Upanishad and Vedanta classes
courses.description: Live weekend classes on Zoom with Swami Sarvananda: the Bhagavad Gita verse by verse over about 200 classes, the Mundaka Upanishad and the Panchadashi, each with time for questions. Students register through the site's form.

free_resources.title: Recordings of Bhagavad Gita and Sanskrit classes
free_resources.description: Downloadable audio of the opening Gita classes from 2020 and 2021, from the introduction and the dhyana verses through chapter one, with links to video recordings and notes for the Sanskrit classes.
